title: The History of Sonic the Hedgehog | Genesis to Movies | Gaming History
description: The full history of Sonic the Hedgehog: the 1991 original, Sonic 2, Sonic Adventure, Sega leaving consoles, Sonic Mania, Frontiers, the movies and the billion dollar franchise.

sections.heading: Gotta go fast
sections.script: A blue blur, a ring counter and a speed that left every other mascot behind. Sonic the Hedgehog is one of the most recognizable characters in gaming, and his story is full of big wins, hard lessons and surprising comebacks. In this video we follow the history of the Sonic series: from the first game on the Sega Genesis in nineteen ninety one, through the golden days of the sixteen bit era, the leap to three dimensions on the Dreamcast, and the moment Sega left the console business. We will also look at Sonic Mania, the modern open world games, the movies that passed one billion dollars at the box office, and the sales milestones that make Sonic one of the biggest franchises ever. Whether you grew up with a Genesis controller or met Sonic in a movie theater, there is something here for you. Ready? Let's go.

sections.heading: Sega needs a mascot
sections.script: In the early nineteen nineties, Sega wanted a mascot that could stand up to Nintendo's Mario. The answer was a blue hedgehog with attitude. The character was designed by Naoto Ohshima, the game was programmed by Yuji Naka, and Hirokazu Yasuhara worked on the game design, together forming the team that became known as Sonic Team. Sonic the Hedgehog was released on the Sega Genesis in North America on June twenty third, nineteen ninety one, and in Japan on July twenty sixth. The game was built around speed, loops, springs and a first level, Green Hill Zone, that fans still know by heart. It became the best selling game on the Genesis, and it turned a company mascot into a global star almost overnight. It helped Sega compete against Nintendo in the fierce console war of the sixteen bit era.

sections.heading: Sonic 2sday
sections.script: The sequel was an even bigger event. Sonic the Hedgehog Two was released on November twenty fourth, nineteen ninety two, in North America and Europe, a Tuesday that Sega famously marketed as Sonic Twosday. Japan had received the game a few days earlier, on November twenty first. The game introduced Tails, the two tailed fox who became Sonic's best friend, along with a split screen race mode and special stages where Sonic collects the Chaos Emeralds. It was developed by Sega Technical Institute, with Yuji Naka and Hirokazu Yasuhara joining from Japan. It was praised for its levels, its visuals and its music, and many fans still say that this is where classic Sonic reached its peak.

sections.heading: The jump to three dimensions
sections.script: As gaming moved into three dimensions, Sonic had to change too. Sonic Adventure was released on the Sega Dreamcast in Japan on December twenty third, nineteen ninety eight, and in North America on September ninth, nineteen ninety nine. It was the first main Sonic game with full three dimensional gameplay, directed by Takashi Iizuka and produced by Yuji Naka, who both still shape the series. The game sold about two and a half million copies by two thousand six and became the best selling title on the Dreamcast. Players ran through cities, forests and ancient ruins, and the game gave the series a new look and a new rhythm. It showed that Sonic could survive the change of era, and it set the template for many of the three dimensional games that followed over the next two decades.

sections.heading: Sega leaves the console race
sections.script: Not every change was a happy one. On January thirty first, two thousand one, Sega announced that it would stop making consoles and become a third party game publisher, and Dreamcast production ended that spring. Suddenly Sonic could appear on machines that were once his biggest rivals. Sonic Adventure Two, released on the Dreamcast in June two thousand one, later came to the Nintendo GameCube, the first time Sega gave Nintendo such a major character on its own hardware. For fans it was a strange moment, but it gave the series a much larger audience. Since then Sonic has appeared on almost every major platform, from home consoles to phones, and the hedgehog has never left the spotlight.

sections.heading: Sonic Mania, a gift for fans
sections.script: After years of mixed reactions to some of the three dimensional games, fans were asking Sega to return to the classic style. In August two thousand seventeen, that wish came true with Sonic Mania, released on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, Xbox One and later on PC. It was led by Christian Whitehead, with art and level design from the studios PagodaWest Games and Headcannon, a team that had grown out of the Sonic fan community. Sonic Mania remixed classic zones such as Green Hill with brand new levels and bosses, and critics praised it as a real return to form for the series. It showed that the old formula still works when it is made with love.

sections.heading: Sonic hits the big screen
sections.script: Sonic also conquered the cinema. The live action Sonic the Hedgehog film arrived in twenty twenty, followed by Sonic the Hedgehog Two on April eighth, twenty twenty two, which broke the record for the best performing video game movie in the United States at that time. Jim Carrey returned as Doctor Robotnik, and critics singled him out for praise. Sonic the Hedgehog Three followed in December twenty twenty four, with Keanu Reeves voicing Shadow the Hedgehog. In January twenty twenty five, Paramount announced that the film series had passed one billion dollars at the worldwide box office. A fourth film is scheduled for March nineteenth, twenty twenty seven, so the movie story is far from over. It is a rare case where a game character found the same success in cinemas that he first found on a console.

sections.heading: Frontiers, Superstars and Shadow
sections.script: The games kept moving too. Sonic Frontiers launched on November eighth, twenty twenty two, and it was the first Sonic game with an open world design, set on the mysterious Starfall Islands. It was led by Takashi Iizuka, the head of Sonic Team, who wanted to evolve the linear three dimensional action of the series into something more open. In October twenty twenty three, Sonic Superstars returned to two dimensional side scrolling on October seventeenth, developed together with the studio Arzest. And on October twenty fifth, twenty twenty four, Sonic X Shadow Generations brought a remastered Sonic Generations together with a new campaign starring Shadow. The series now tries many styles at once.

sections.heading: One and a half billion and counting
sections.script: How big is Sonic today? In its report for March twenty twenty two, Sega said the franchise had passed one and a half billion sales and downloads, counting both premium games and free to play mobile titles. A large share of that comes from mobile, where Sonic Dash alone passed five hundred million downloads. That makes Sonic one of the biggest series in Sega's history, far ahead of the company's other franchises. From a Genesis cartridge in nineteen ninety one to phones, consoles, movies and toys, the hedgehog has kept running for over three decades, and nothing suggests he will slow down soon. The speed and the attitude simply never go out of style, and every new generation of players seems to find its own favorite Sonic game along the way.

sections.heading: Your favorite Sonic
sections.script: From a mascot built to rival Mario to a global entertainment brand, Sonic has had an unforgettable journey. Which Sonic game is your favorite, the classic Genesis era, the Dreamcast adventures, Sonic Mania or the new open zone games? And which character should get the next big spotlight, Tails, Knuckles or Shadow? Tell us in the comments. If you enjoyed this history, like the video and subscribe for more gaming history, and we will see you in the next video. Keep running, keep collecting rings and keep having fun. See you next time.
